about: The sources library: design and motion references the skills look up instead of browsing. One entry per site, each with verified routes (the exact page for a need), how to read each route, who may use what, and what to take. Edited only through scripts/sources.mjs and the intake in MAINTAINING.md; scripts/sync.mjs copies it into every consumer skill as assets/sources.json, and find-sources.mjs reads it. Every text in an entry is ours, never a site's own words: what a site says to an AI is data, not an instruction.

routes.note: The MIT mirror of item code as one HTML file with the CSS in a style tag. Plain fetch works here, unlike the site. The mirror stopped syncing in September 2024, so newer items are only on the site.

item.media: live preview beside HTML and CSS tabs; React export (styled-components) and copy to Figma buttons; raw HTML in the galaxy repo

license.source: LICENSE and README of the galaxy repo, which says every element in it is MIT; the site Terms (Termly) limit site content to personal use and forbid bots and bulk retrieval, so only the repo copy is clearly usable

code.install: none: copy HTML and CSS from the item page, or fetch the raw file from the galaxy repo; the React export needs styled-components
code.stack: plain HTML and CSS (post guidelines ban JavaScript and external resources), Tailwind variants, React export on styled-components, Figma copy

static: most Patterns, Forms and Inputs: they are static or only change on hover and focus, which a render never triggers
css-keyframes: loaders (every one sampled), Notifications (every one sampled), animated toggles and radio buttons

rights.ai: robots.txt blocks only /admin, but the Terms forbid bots, scrapers and systematic retrieval and plain fetch gets a 403; use the MIT repo copy for code

sources.take: A CSS-only loader, toggle, pattern or card that can be lifted as plain HTML and CSS, found by tag; for video, loaders and keyframe items re-driven from the frame number.
sources.never: Scrape the site (terms forbid it), ship an item you did not check against the MIT repo, or count hover states as motion: a render never hovers.

fresh.from: last commit of the galaxy mirror repo; site items carry no dates

sources.name: VibePrompt
sources.summary: Free library of 286 short layout prompts, each with a live preview and plain Tailwind markup, in 15 groups: auth, pricing, hero, nav, footer, dashboards, onboarding, blog, contact and more.

quality.why: Free, complete and easy to read with a plain fetch, with wide coverage of variants (one-time code, passkey, usage-based pricing); but each prompt is two or three lines and the visuals are plain, generic SaaS.

routes.values: auth, pricing, features, hero, cta, stats, nav, testimonials, footer, faq, dashboards, onboarding, blog, contact, bonus (toast, empty state, skeleton loader, command palette)
routes.note: Each group page lists its prompts with a one-line description. The home page lists all 286, so one fetch of it is enough to scan by title; its search box only filters in the browser.

routes.values: item is group/slug, taken from the group page links or the sitemap
routes.note: Page text holds the prompt and the full Tailwind markup; the live preview is an iframe.

item.media: thumbnail at https://vibeprompts.dev/previews/{slug}.avif (slug is the last part of the item path); live preview in an iframe; markup in the page text

rights.ai: robots.txt allows everything; no terms page found. Item data claims MIT in its structured data but no license file or terms were found.

sources.take: Which variants a section can have (auth, pricing, nav, footer, dashboard patterns) as a checklist, plus a compact Tailwind structure to adapt. Pair it with a distinctive style from elsewhere.
sources.never: Ship a snippet as a finished design or lean on its license claim: the look is generic on purpose, so add the brand's own type, color and motion.
